sentences.text: Rosey Greenwood was asked to pay £1,906 because she took more than five minutes to pay for parking "I was completely on edge, every single day," said Rosey Greenwood.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "I had letters coming through - I had debt collectors after me." Two years ago, Rosey was being told to pay £1,906 because she had taken too long to pay for parking.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Rosey had paid every single time she parked at the Copeland Street car park in Derby, and had bank records to prove it.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: But Rosey had unknowingly broken the car park's terms and conditions, which stipulated that drivers must pay within five minutes of entering.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Rosey could not afford to pay £1,906 - she was due to get married and also saving up to buy her first home.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: As she prepared to fight the case in court, her fiance emailed the BBC and asked us to "shed some light" on what was happening .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The case was then raised in Parliament , external by Derby North MP Catherine Atkinson, who described the charges - which had caught out countless other motorists - as a "five-minute rip-off charge".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The parking sector subsequently banned the five-minute payment rule by updating its code of practice , external , but the government is going further by bringing in a statutory Private Parking Code of Practice.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "These charges leave people feeling ripped off and out of pocket, so I'm putting a stop to them," Prime Minister Andy Burnham said , external on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: But will the new code actually put the brakes on "rip-off" parking charges?
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said parking charges left people "feeling ripped off" The government's new Private Parking Code of Practice was laid out in Parliament on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: It sets out standards that parking operators must follow.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Housing and communities minister Florence Eshalomi said , external the new code "will give drivers a range of rights and protections to make these unfair practices a thing of the past".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The code is now subject to a 40-day period of parliamentary scrutiny, during which MPs and peers can object before it is formally issued.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The code will then come into force 21 calendar days from the point of issue.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The five-minute payment rule - as stipulated on this sign - had already been banned by the parking sector itself In places, the code appears to be very similar to the private parking sector's existing code of practice , external .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: For example, Eshalomi said drivers would "now have a guaranteed minimum five minutes to decide whether to park", known as the consideration period.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: However, the sector's code already gives drivers a minimum consideration period of five minutes, so this does not appear to be new.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code also gives drivers a 10-minute grace period , external in which to leave a car park following the end of their permitted stay.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: However, the sector's code already gives drivers a 10-minute grace period, so this does not appear to be new either.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code sets the maximum parking charge at £100, or £60 if paid within a fortnight.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This is also the same as in the sector's code.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code states charges should be reduced to £20 on appeal , external under four circumstances: not displaying a parking permit despite having a valid one, entering the wrong vehicle registration into a parking machine, not entering a registration at all, and not displaying a Blue Badge despite having one.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The sector's code already said charges should be reduced to £20 under those circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Parking operators will also still be allowed to add a £70 debt recovery fee , external to each parking charge if drivers do not pay, as well as court fees and legal costs.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: In contrast, the sector's code said these charges should be reduced to £20.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government's code says parking operators who do not comply will lose access to DVLA vehicle keeper data, meaning they will no longer be able to issue parking charges.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This is meant to happen already, because parking operators need to be members of one of two trade associations in order to access DVLA data, and they can theoretically lose their membership if they break the rules.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Campaigners claim this has not happened in practice, but the government insists it will happen in future.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: There will also be what the government describes as a "fully independent Scrutiny and Oversight Board".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Jack Cousens, head of roads policy at the AA, said the benefit of the new code was that it was backed by the government, rather than the parking sector itself.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "That means, if there are any changes to be made, it will come via the government and indeed via the independent scrutiny panel," he added.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "Up until now, the private industry have held the pen on changing the code of practice.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Now the pen is firmly in the hand of the government." Lynda Eagan does not believe the new code will lead to fewer parking charge notices being issued Both the AA and RAC have welcomed the statutory code of practice - which they campaigned for - but believe it does not go far enough.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: For example, the AA believes there needs to be a single and independent appeals process.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "Drivers need to have confidence that when they are making their representations, it's being heard by an independent body, as opposed to the private parking operators and their trade bodies marking their own homework," Cousens said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The AA also believes the government needs to find an alternative to debt recovery fees and charges, which often "spiral" into the threat of court action and County Court Judgments.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: This was how Rosey was asked to pay a total of £1,906 for 10 parking charges, and also how Hannah Robinson was asked to pay £11,390 .
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The RAC shares the same concerns.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "We've long called for the banning of debt recovery fees being added on top of parking charge notices, and a single independent appeals body to replace the two industry-run ones, but neither have been included [in the code] which is disappointing," head of policy Simon Williams said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The government said it was "consulting as soon as possible next year on private parking debt recovery fees, including on whether to cut an existing £70 cap or scrap the fees altogether".
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Parking campaigner Lynda Eagan, who helped Rosey, is sceptical about how much has changed.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "I've been screaming at the TV every time I see someone saying 'we've got these new things'," she said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "They've tweaked a few things here and there, but it's not actually going to make an awful lot of difference to people.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "How, when not much has really changed, is that going to reduce the number of PCNs [parking charge notices]?" In response, a Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government spokesperson said: "We don't accept these claims.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: We've introduced a new Private Parking Code of Practice that will have statutory force and independent oversight.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The AA is more optimistic.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "We are hopeful that it could make some difference to some drivers, and we hope that it stops some of the more spurious claims being stopped at source, but we will be watching," Cousens said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: The International Parking Community said "any changes must remain fair to motorists while staying workable" The two trade associations for parking operators, which wrote the sector's existing code, are reading and reviewing the government's changes.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: Alison Tooze, chief policy officer at the British Parking Association, said: "Overall, the code strikes the right balance between stronger protections for motorists and effective parking management, helping keep communities, businesses and local economies moving." She said retaining a £100 parking charge was important.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: "Evidence shows that meaningful deterrents support compliance and good behaviours, helping ensure parking remains available for those who need it and enabling parking to be managed effectively," she added.
sentences.article_title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the International Parking Community (IPC) said: "The IPC has long supported a code that raises standards, and we are now reviewing it in detail to understand what it means for motorists, landowners and operators alike.

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.

sentences.text: Google's translation service handles one trillion words per month "Il pleut des cordes," say the French when it's raining hard.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "It's raining ropes," is the direct translation.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: It's the kind of idiom which can trip up an AI translator.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "You can imagine the dilemma this throws AI into," says François Yvon, a research director specialised in automatic translation with the French National Centre for Scientific Research CNRS.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: He says a well-trained system will know that ropes are not literally falling from the sky and use the English phrase "it's raining cats and dogs".
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "But is it going to find the equivalent when it's translating into Indonesian?" asks Yvon.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: A comment on the weather is pretty low-risk, but more and more translation is being done by machines, and on topics with higher stakes than the weather.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: In April, Google said people are now translating , external one trillion words a month with Google Translate.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: That doesn't count the others: DeepL, Microsoft, Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, not to mention made-to-measure corporate translation systems.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Direct sales of machine translation , external (i.e. outside general AI subscriptions) were worth an estimated $1.4bn (£1bn) last year.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "For an encyclopedia it's different.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: A wrong fact can sit there for years and get cited by journalists and AI systems," he says.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: With more than 10,000 published pieces, mostly into Spanish, Portuguese and English, OKA is, Zimmerman says, the single largest contributor of translated articles to the collaborative online encyclopedia.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Which is something it absolutely could not have become without AI.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "Translating 10,000 articles the traditional way would cost millions.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: In our process, the AI produces the draft, then a human translator checks every sentence," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: But that human input is required less and less.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "The machine output is now good enough that skipping the human entirely has become a serious option, and a real temptation across the industry.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Two or three years ago, with tools like DeepL, our translators still rewrote a good chunk of every draft.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "Today the prose often doesn't need fixing at all.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: So, the question is no longer whether AI translation is good, it clearly is, but whether it's good enough to remove the human," says Zimmermann.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Not yet, translators argue.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Ariella Baltié is a translator and legal expert specialised in translating court documents from English into French.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: She was contacted recently by someone who'd already translated his documents with AI, asking her to check them.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "There were two major errors right at the beginning," she said.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: The AI had translated "Le demandeur" (the plaintiff) as "the requester".
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "Totally awkward for legal papers," says Baltié.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: When the AI saw "Madame X, épouse Y" (Ms X, wife of Y'), it came up with "Ms X marries Y".
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: In other words, it mistook a noun for a verb, completely losing the meaning of the phrase.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: The consequences of mistranslation in the legal sphere can be serious.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: In the US, for example, errors in machine-translated asylum applications have led to delays in the release of detainees.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Ariella Baltié specialises in legal translation work Accuracy is a matter of life and death in the medical field.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "The units for dosages and blood tests often include Greek letters," says Carol Bereuter, who is a specialist in medical translations.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: She came across one automatically-translated text that had translated the greek letter μ as milli (one thousandth) instead of micro (one millionth).
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: If you give someone a milligram when it's meant to be a microgram, you are giving them a thousand times the dose," points out Bereuter.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: She also makes the point that, as AI translators have got better, catching errors has got more difficult.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "Whereas in the past, with things like Google Translate, the sentence would jump out at you because there'd be a grammatical error or it would sound clunky, today it sounds perfectly legitimate.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: So the errors are a lot harder to spot." Carol Bereuter is a specialist in medical translations "If it's something that will bear your signature, there's a risk for your reputation.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: And if decisions are going to be taken on the basis of a translation concerning a medical procedure, a contract you might sign or a major purchase you might make, the risk is even greater," warns François Yvon.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Even sentences that seem quite clear to a human can trip up an AI service, he says.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "When you have words with different meanings, it's usually very clear for a human which one applies because they understand the context, but when a machine translator comes across the sentence 'translate into Polish', for example, it is quite capable of deciding it must be all about shoe cream, says Yvon.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Context is often crucial.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: If an AI translator hasn't grasped that we're talking about a football match it is liable to mis-translate "taking a corner".
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Last year OKA ran a study, funded by Wikimedia.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: It studied 119 articles, 10 language pairs and more than 1,000 hours of translator work.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "27% of the AI-generated text still got corrected before publication.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Three quarters of those corrections were errors the AI introduced, and 5 to 6% of errors changed the meaning of the original text," says Zimmerman.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Eradicating those errors is likely to be challenging.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "As things stand, I think the fundamental way these systems function makes it quite hard to imagine how they could become 100% reliable," says François Yvon.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: This is because probability is a crucial part of the way AI translates each word rather than another and what is probably correct is not the same as what is correct.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Especially in the realm of something as subtle and surprising as language.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: He thinks a new generation of tech will be an improvement.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "We will see translation systems that are increasingly capable of evaluating what they do and correcting themselves using different AI tools simultaneously: one to do the translation, a second to criticize it and a third to produce a new version, for example." But perhaps the big moment will be when AI can show doubt.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "The real breakthrough won't come until these systems are not merely capable of translating but also of telling us when they're not sure," Yvon says.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Neither did thousands of other residents in Homer, Alaska, who later discovered a  start-up called Rainmaker conducted an experiment in that region using cloud-seeding technology.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The company, based in El Segundo California, claims it produced 19 million US gallons of water in the sky in three hours.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: This approach to weather modification, now more than 80-years-old, involves using planes and drones to disperse compounds such as silver iodide into clouds to form ice crystals.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Gravity then pulls those crystals to the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The technology, though, needs ideal climate environments, such as mountainous or cold regions such as Alaska.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman, the Alaska director of the Center for Biological Diversity, isn't just concerned Homer residents weren't widely alerted to these experiments.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He's sceptical about what was shot into the clouds, and questions how safe it was for both residents and their habitat.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It doesn't appear that there was any downstream monitoring to verify that this silver iodide didn't impact the environment," he says.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman adds, "Having a company come in to do this seeding isn't going to solve our water woes, and it feels like a distraction from solving the urgent issues related to water conservation." Concerns are mounting about the challenges surrounding water security.

sentences.text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in July "our world is using freshwater faster than it can be replenished , external ", which echoes reports noting how the past five years have led to the driest period for global rivers , external in more than three decades.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).

sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "Never in my wildest dreams did I think that a solar project would be on my farm," Cargil says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Looking back now, he calls it a blessing.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: The lease, which pays Cargil $200,000 (£150,000) a year, has let him keep his farm running through a punishing drought.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Solar farms can stretch out across the flat lands of Texas On hot afternoons, when demand for power peaks, solar is now regularly supplying around a third of the electricity used across Texas, says Mark Stover, executive director of the Texas Solar and Storage Association.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He says that the solar boom is being driven by two main things.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Firstly, it is cheap and quick to connect solar farms to Texas' power grid, which is separate to the rest of the US.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Secondly, Texas has a huge and growing appetite for electricity, driven by a burgeoning population.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2025, Texas's population increased by 15.8%, , external making it one of the fastest-growing states in the nation.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We need a whole lot of power in Texas, and we need it quickly," Stover says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Solar has also become inexpensive.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: James Scott, vice president of project development at OCI, says the technology has had years of small manufacturing gains that brought the price down to the point where it is now the cheapest way to generate power in the state.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "No one would have believed that 20 years ago," Scott says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Once a project is built, he says, the price of the electricity it produces can be fixed for decades, since the fuel, sunlight, is free.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We'll charge you $40 a megawatt hour for the next 25 years," Scott says, adding that large buyers such as Amazon and Apple value being able to lock in a price for that long.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: By contrast, new coal plants in the US produce power at nearly $90 megawatts per hour, says the Energy Information Administration.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Farmers have become central to that growth because solar developers need large stretches of flat land.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Stover says the industry is now paying out multigenerational income to families through leases that typically run 25 to 30 years and rise in value each year, letting some retire, set up family trusts, or simply keep a farm solvent.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Stover argues solar's footprint is smaller than critics assume.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "The industry is utilizing less than 0.15% of Texas land," he says.

sentences.text: In Franklin County, in northeast Texas, a small group of residents has spent the past few years fighting its growth.

sentences.text: BF Hicks, a local lawyer whose family has owned land in the county since the 1800s, says he watched neighbours sign 30-year leases with solar companies and bulldozers clear centuries-old oak trees near his property.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He describes a summer when smoke from burning cleared land hung over his town for weeks.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "It got real personal," he says, when a solar farm was built next to his family's cemetery.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: His relatives have been buried here dating back two centuries.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: David Truesdale, a retired federal law enforcement agent who moved to the county to get away from city life, says he became involved after learning that a neighbouring solar project would sit near his home.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: And that under Texan law no environmental review was required.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We're destroying the world as we're trying to save it," Truesdale says of the land clearing he has seen.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He also points to the large lithium-ion battery units installed alongside many solar farms, drawing a comparison to fires that have occasionally engulfed similar batteries in electric bikes.

sentences.text: "If one of those things catches fire, they go off in series, so each one will progressively cause another one to go off," he says.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Freddo the robot in action at Vsim Freddo the robot walks across the office and takes a plastic bottle offered by a staff member.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This year, close to 100 million foreigners are expected to come to Spain, making it the second most-visited country in the world, just behind France.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are signs that the heat is becoming too much for some travellers.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, this summer tested their tolerance of heat, with the country registering a record-breaking 61 days of heatwaves that continued into early September.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Toledo repeatedly saw temperatures in excess of 40C.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company VisiToledo.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he would like to see more shade and drinking fountains available.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He says the heat has started to change the timing of the tourist season, bringing many more visitors during the cooler months of spring and autumn.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Warmer summers have also encouraged the so-called "coolcation" trend, whereby Spanish travellers seek out cooler areas to spend their holidays, typically in the north of the country.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was a disaster, both in terms of the lives lost and the impact on businesses, on workers, employers and ordinary people," says Laura Llácer Álvarez, manager of the Fepeval federation of industrial parks in the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Germanwatch, an independent environmental organisation, ranked Spain the world's 20th most affected country in its climate risk index for 2024, just behind Nigeria and Mali.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are those who see an upside for the economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "Climate change affects how we produce, how we invest and how we consume," says Julián Cubero, head of economics of climate change at economic think tank BBVA Research.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He points to how heat can act as a drag on economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We all work worse when it's hot," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he adds, a greener economy can create new jobs with greater productivity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The key is to realise that if we don't act, growth will slow down, and if it's handled right it can become an opportunity," he says.

sentences.text: The Green Party of England and Wales has been declared a racist organisation by the Board of Deputies of British Jews.

sentences.article_title: Political battle intensifies within Labour over Rosebank oil field

sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Campaigners argue this gives renters greater security and confidence to ask for repairs, without fearing they could be evicted if they raise concerns.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Lewis Wilson from the NUS says the legislation has given students more freedom to move out when they want However, greater flexibility for students to leave tenancies also means less certainty for landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The act did introduce a specific ground , external for landlords to evict a group of students at the end of the academic year if they intend to re-let the property to students.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association, says the bigger problem for student landlords is if their tenants choose to move out earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He argues this is a bigger risk for students - who may fall out with their housemates or drop out of university - than, for example, families, who are less likely to want to move out after just a few months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says the end of fixed-term tenancies means student houses could be left empty over the summer after courses finish - or even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He adds that it is now more difficult for student landlords to rent a house for just a few months as they don't know how long the tenants will stay and can't guarantee it will be available for students again in the autumn.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says it's early days for the new legislation and many landlords are taking this year as a test to see how these issues play out in practice.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, he warns that some may choose to increase the monthly rent they charge to cover the risk of their properties being empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: In some cases, he says landlords may even sell up or stop renting to students, reducing supply and pushing up prices.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue Lawes thinks the changes mean many student landlords will put up their rent Sue Lawes, who rents three shared houses to students in Norwich, is worried about the changes.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While Sue says she doesn't want to put up her prices, if her houses end up being empty over the summer because students decide to end their tenancy after their final exams she says she may have to.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She has already brought forward the start of her tenancy agreements to August instead of September to try and reduce the risks of this.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, she says if her tenants move out earlier in the year she would struggle to make a profit, whilst covering costs including her mortgage, council tax and utility standing charges when the properties are empty.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She argues higher monthly rents would mean bigger upfront costs for students and higher overall costs for those who do choose to carry on renting over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue stresses that she supports the aim of the legislation to give tenants greater security and that students should be able to move out if their landlord is not carrying out repairs.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But she wants landlords to be allowed to offer fixed-term contracts to students in line with the academic year to avoid properties being left empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords are going to find it very, very hard to absorb those void periods," she says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords will put prices up and students are going to pay." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.
