sentences.text: But in other areas Green councillors are yet to specify where they stand on the issue, meaning local alliances appear more vulnerable to collapse.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: The issue is the most acute in nine local authorities where Greens are key partners in power-sharing arrangements, such as making up majorities that enable budgets to be passed and policy decisions to be made.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: These include Sheffield City Council, Warwick District Council and Lewes District Council, three authorities where Labour and the Greens are in direct coalition.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: The other areas where the Greens play a key role are: West Oxfordshire District Council, Stafford Borough Council, Havant Borough Council, Broadland District Council, Derbyshire Dales District Council and Wealden District Council.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: In other areas, Green councillors are not central to local alliances continuing to function.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: These include Runnymede Borough Council, where Green councillors have left the local ruling alliance folllowing Labour's ultimatum.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: In some areas, such as Lewes, Wealden, Broadland, West Sussex and North Somerset, local Green groups have distanced themselves from their party's Zionism policy, or said they do not agree with it.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: But other Green groups are yet to publicly respond to Labour's demands, meaning there is greater uncertainty over the future of their co-operation with the party.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: In Stafford, the power-sharing arrangement means the Greens have one cabinet member on the authority, councillor Tony Pearce, who holds the climate change portfolio.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Councillor Pearce has been contacted for comment but has not yet responded.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: The leader of the Stafford Green group, Doug Rouxel told the BBC they were "formulating a response" to Labour's letter which they would like to put to party members first.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Labour confirmed the if the Greens refused to reject the Zionism policy, a process would then be triggered to remove Pearce from his cabinet position in Stafford.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Elsewhere, the leader of the Labour group on the Green-led Lewes District Council has resigned from the party, following his own party's ultimatum.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Chris Collier, who has been contacted for comment, will now sit as an independent cabinet member on the Labour-Green alliance that was formed to run the council in May 2023.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: The BBC has been told Collier did not agree with the tone of Labour's ultimatum to the Green Party over the Zionism policy.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: The "Zionism is racism" motion was passed by members of the Green Party of England and Wales at its annual conference in Brighton last month.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: The policy motion adopted by members said Zionism was an ideology that supported an "ethnonationalist Jewish state" that had led to the "disenfranchisement and destruction" of Palestinians.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: It backed the creation of a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: It has led to a backlash from Jewish groups, as well as criticism from senior Green figures, including four of its five MPs.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Green leader Zack Polanski, who skipped the conference vote to unsuccessfully campaign for election in a Westminster by-election, has said he wants to see the "imperfect" motion amended in future.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Labour councillors require the approval of the party's NEC before entering into local tie-ups.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: According to the party's rulebook, local groups must also "stand down" from power-sharing arrangements when asked to do so by their regional office.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: By contrast, the Green Party of England and Wales allows local groups to make the final decision on where and whether to share power locally.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: A Green Party spokesperson said: "For the Labour government to conflate criticism of Israel with antisemitism is disappointing and wrong.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: "Trying to tell local parties what to do and who they can work with is undemocratic." Additional reporting by Victoria Walton, Jennie Aitken, Hannah Miller, Vikki Irwin, Emily Hudson, Lucinda Adam.
sentences.article_title: Green councillors face Labour deadline to disown Zionism policy

sentences.text: Households will need to earn less than £110,000 to qualify for the government's new loan scheme for first-time buyers, or £140,000 for homes bought in London.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: As first reported by The Times , external , the earnings limits are expected to be confirmed at the Budget next week.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Your First Home scheme will offer government-backed equity loans worth 20% of new-build properties in England bought from participating developers.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The loans, which will also be subject to an initial interest-free period, are designed to help people buy a home with deposits as low as 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Previous schemes to help first-time buyers did not restrict eligibility by income but faced criticism for stoking house prices by allowing relatively wealthy households to borrow more.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Unveiling the Your First Home Scheme at last month's Labour conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would focus on those who "really need support".
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Times reported that ministers had initially decided to set the earnings limits at £90,000 for homes outside outside London and £110,000 in the capital, before concluding this would deny access to too many middle-earning couples, such as teachers and nurses.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The government has also argued that the scheme will help to boost housebuilding, after ministers conceded they are set to miss a target to build 1.5 million homes in England by the next election.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Labour has said the scheme will be funded by within existing government budgets, but is yet to provide details of which other areas will see their spending cut.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Developers taking part in the scheme will also be asked to contribute towards running costs.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Home Builders Federation, which represents developers, has welcomed  the plans and urged the government to move quickly to set up the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: The Conservatives have however branded the proposals a "colossal admission of failure" of Labour's housebuilding record, and expressed concerns that the new developer levy could push up the price of new homes.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Like the Help to Buy scheme launched under the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government, the scheme will use equity loans, which are linked to changes in the value of properties they are used to purchase.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: That scheme, which initially ran between 2013 and 2021, enabled all home purchasers to put down a 5% deposit on a newly built home worth up to £600,000.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: Up to 20% of the cost of the home was funded by a shared equity loan, which was interest-free for the first five years.
sentences.article_title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

sentences.text: A second version of that scheme, which ran from 2021 to 2023, restricted access to first-time buyers and applied regional-level price caps to the properties could be bought under the programme.

sentences.text: Anthony Lee and his wife Laura pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have received suspended prison sentences after they admitted to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Anthony Lee used "inside information" emerging from a private meeting called by then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to bet on the general election date months before it took place, Southwark Crown Court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Lee and his wife Laura stood to win more than £23,000 had their cheating not been uncovered, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Lee was sentenced to 10 months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, while his wife was sentenced to four months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for a year.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Amy Hind, a former Tory party employee who was working as an NHS business support manager, was also sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for a year, after previously pleading guilty to cheating on the date of the election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Judge Tony Baumgartner, sentencing the three of them, said their conduct "risked undermining" the confidence the public has in the Conservative Party "as an institution", "undermining trust in the democratic process" and the "integrity of the gambling system".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trio were among several people charged with betting offences by the Gambling Commission.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trials of other defendants will take place next year and in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Former Conservative MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Sunak's decision to call a general election for July 2024 was a surprise to many, including several Conservative MPs, who were expecting an autumn date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard that Sunak held a private Downing Street meeting on 10 March of that year to discuss possible dates.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Neither Lee nor his wife attended the meeting, but the couple began betting online on the election being held in July or between July and September, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner described Anthony Lee as a "central figure" in the preparation of the general election, who sat at a group of desks within Tory HQ known as the "God Pod".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Representing Lee, barrister Richard Pratt said his client did not concretely know the working date of the election, saying it "still represented a gamble from his point of view".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The barrister told the court: "It was always possible the prime minister could change his mind." Pratt said there "wasn't any direct manipulation" by the defendant.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Laura Lee worked for the Tories as their "head of international" and had been selected as the party candidate for Bristol North West for the election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner said she had no involvement in the election planning and her access to information "came predominantly" from her husband.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard Hind's husband Anthony worked as a deputy digital director for the Conservatives but did not place any bets himself.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner said Hind's husband "was party to emails relating to the forthcoming general election and was one potential source of your inside information".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The judge later said "someone else who worked within the heart of CCHQ" could have given her the "highly confidential" information.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The court heard Hind placed four bets and made three further unsuccessful attempts to place bets.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The unsuccessful attempts were for £767, £700 and £750.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Baumgartner described them all as having expressed remorse for their actions.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: The trio are now subject to a 12-month prohibited activity requirement, banning them from accessing or using online gambling websites or applications.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Anthony Lee was ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and pay more than £6,600 in compensation to a betting company, while Laura Lee must carry out 40 hours of unpaid work and pay £4,265.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Hind was ordered to complete 50 hours of unpaid work.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Katharine Diamond, General Counsel of regulators the Gambling Commission, reacted to the sentencing of the trio by saying "justice has been served".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: She described the case as "a first of its kind" and said it demonstrated the commission's "commitment to protecting the integrity of betting markets".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife receive suspended sentences over election bets

sentences.text: Burnham will appear on the show with his friend Steve Rotheram, the Labour mayor of the Liverpool City Region Prime Minister Andy Burnham has defended his decision to appear on a celebrity episode of Channel 4 hit show Gogglebox after opposition leader Kemi Badenoch said she was "amazed" he had time to do it.

sentences.article_title: PM defends Gogglebox appearance after Badenoch criticism

sentences.article_title: PM defends Gogglebox appearance after Badenoch criticism

sentences.text: "Steve and I are proud to do it.

sentences.text: "I'm trying to give the country a lift - trying to give the county some hope.

sentences.text: Cleveland PCC Matt Storey said Cleveland Police was still waiting for the extra funding promised by the home secretary in August.

sentences.text: Shabana Mahmood pledged the cash in light of challenges faced by the force following the deaths, which followed a pursuit on the A66 at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on 22 August.
sentences.article_title: Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner

sentences.text: Five young men were also killed.
sentences.article_title: Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner

sentences.text: The Home Office said the force would receive the £2m it had been promised by the end of November.
sentences.article_title: Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner

sentences.text: During the fatal crash, a Volkswagen Passat in which the five young men were travelling hit an oncoming marked Cleveland Police vehicle on the dual carriageway near Middlesbrough at about 03:39 BST.
sentences.article_title: Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner

sentences.text: Officers PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died at the scene.
sentences.article_title: Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner

sentences.text: The occupants of the VW Passat, which was travelling the wrong way down the A66 at South Bank - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, and 17-year-olds Theo Rae and Cole Robert Worthy - were also killed.
sentences.article_title: Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner

sentences.text: Andy Burnham said military aircraft will be used to tackle wildfires as he tries to ensure the UK is "on the front foot" following a summer of devastating blazes.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Civilian fire services in all four nations will be able to request the support of the Royal Air Force's Chinook helicopters and A400M planes to fight wildfires on tough terrain such as remote moorland and steep hillsides.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: As he hosted the UK's first summit on wildfires, the prime minister outlined initial steps to "improve our response" after the country "lived through a summer that we've never seen before".
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Burnham said this also includes better equipment for firefighters and improved land management to stop fires from spreading.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: After a record-breaking summer, the government's "wildfire resilience summit" in Liverpool on Friday discussed how to prevent, respond to and recover from such blazes.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: There have been 1,350 wildfires in England and Wales this year, an all-time high and up by more than 300 on last year and more than 1,000 on 2024, according to figures from the National Fire Chiefs Council .
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Records for the number of reported wildfires were also broken in 2022 and 2025 - but the UK's Climate Change Committee has warned the risk will rise in the coming decades.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said this was the first time the RAF's Chinooks and the four-engine A400Ms were being equipped to tackle wildfires.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Some areas struggled with no air assistance in the summer.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: RAF Chinook crews have already helped respond , external to wildfires in Cyprus.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Chinooks have practised picking up and dropping water from firefighting buckets in Portland harbour, UK In addition to military aircraft, the government said it would also spend £45m on wildfire-specific personal protective equipment for firefighters on the ground.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: It is lighter than current firefighting equipment which is designed for fires in buildings and not meant to be worn for a long time, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Ministers are also pledging a £25m scheme from April 2027 to April 2029 to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they are natural firebreaks, and financial support for farmers to fireproof their land such as by digging ponds.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: "The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high," a briefing ahead of the summit said, following a temporary ban on disposable BBQs .
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Burnham met fire chiefs, local leaders and experts from tech companies at the summit, also attended by Communities Secretary Angela Rayner.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: He said: "I think too often in the past we've been playing catch up, and today is trying about trying to get on the front foot and recognise that the summer we've just had is likely to be a more regular situation going forward.
sentences.article_title: Military aircraft to help get UK 'on front foot' to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: "So make ourselves that bit stronger when it comes to the summer of 2027, and then indeed summers beyond." Burnham earlier told reporters that fire and rescue services were "stretched" this summer and firefighters had worked in "extremely difficult conditions" before committing to providing better equipment.

sentences.text: A clinical trial has been launched in the UK which scientists hope could cut years from the search for new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: It will test multiple drugs simultaneously, starting with two repurposed medicines already used to treat type 2 diabetes and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The study will examine whether the drugs can lessen symptoms such as memory and thinking problems, and help people maintain their quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Angela Bucksey, 67, from Cambridgeshire, was diagnosed with Alzheimer's in January and is the first person to begin treatment on the trial, called AD-SMART.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We have Alzheimer's in the family," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "My mother had it and my aunts, so it was a disappointment rather than a shock when I was diagnosed because I knew it would restrict my life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "But I was determined that it wasn't going to define me." Angela said she felt empowered joining the trial because "at least you are doing something".
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "Instead of just sitting there, you're standing up and saying, I will fight back." Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600,000 people in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham, whose father died from Alzheimer's last month, said he knew how it felt to lose a loved one to dementia, and had seen first-hand the devastating impact of the disease on families.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "That's why I'm proud to see this trial being launched in the UK, so that cutting-edge treatments can reach patients here as soon as possible," he said.

sentences.text: The AD-SMART study is what's known as a multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial where several treatments are tested simultaneously, with the results compared with one group of participants taking a placebo or dummy.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: This means those involved have a higher likelihood of getting an active treatment than in a traditional trial.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: If any drug isn't showing benefit it can be dropped quickly and a new treatment added in its place - the approach has been used successfully in cancer and motor neurone disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The two initial drugs being tested are metformin, used to treat type 2 diabetes, and atomoxetine, for ADHD, which were selected by an international panel of experts.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "For too long, Alzheimer's research has moved at the pace of one drug, one trial, one answer - sometimes taking a decade or more before we know if we've found something that works," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We are applying advances from cancer and other conditions to accelerate testing of treatments for people with Alzheimer's disease." For the drugs to be successful, the study has to show that they have beneficial effects on thinking and the ability to carry out everyday activities.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Hayley lost her job as a teaching assistant last October, after being told she was unfit to work Hayley Locksley was 11 years old when she started her periods and excruciating pain became part of her life.

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred will be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.

sentences.text: A software developer became so frustrated by the amount of rubbish he saw dumped along roadsides that he built an AI-powered "litter dashcam" to expose the scale of the problem.

sentences.text: Robin Bennett, from Shrewsbury, developed the Roadside Litter app after noticing what he believed was a growing amount of litter while driving around the county.
sentences.article_title: Weary driver creates AI 'litter-tracking dashcam'

sentences.text: The technology has already logged more than 3,000 litter reports in Shropshire and more than 28,000 across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Weary driver creates AI 'litter-tracking dashcam'

sentences.text: He is now sharing the data with anti-litter campaign group Clean Up Britain in the hope it will encourage action, while Shropshire Council said it was exploring ways to improve litter management on some of the county's busiest roads.
sentences.article_title: Weary driver creates AI 'litter-tracking dashcam'

sentences.text: Bennett, who runs a software company in Telford, said he found the amount of rubbish on local roads "really depressing" and wanted to understand whether the issue was unique to Shropshire or part of a wider national problem.
sentences.article_title: Weary driver creates AI 'litter-tracking dashcam'

sentences.text: After approaching Clean Up Britain to ask how he could help, he went on to develop what he describes as a "litter dashcam" that records rubbish spotted from a vehicle.
sentences.article_title: Weary driver creates AI 'litter-tracking dashcam'

sentences.text: "My software company's created an app, which essentially is a litter dashcam," he said.
sentences.article_title: Weary driver creates AI 'litter-tracking dashcam'

sentences.text: Bennett said: "I've got a phone holder stuck to the dashboard, I've put my phone in securely.
sentences.article_title: Weary driver creates AI 'litter-tracking dashcam'

sentences.text: Elon Musk has said his company SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service, after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved.

sentences.text: Anthony Horan (left) and Ashley Hanley (right) from North East Lincolnshire trace criminals who illegally dump waste A discarded microwave, a mattress sodden by the rain and even a pile of used syringes.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: The reality of illegally dumped waste sits before me in a colossal mound next to the side of a motorway.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: For the team I'm with, this is a jigsaw waiting to be pieced together and solved as they try to identify the criminal culprits.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: It does not take long for Anthony Horan and Ashley Hanley from North East Lincolnshire Council to find answers within the mountain of waste on the side of the Brocklesby Interchange near Grimsby.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: They tell me it is a goldmine of clues.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: "I'm gobsmacked at the amount of evidence in this one," Anthony Horan, who works as a senior environmental health practitioner for the authority.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: "I'm disgusted at the needles.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: I've never found this amount ever." Numerous syringes, some used, were found strewn within the heap A number of times during the interview we pause after spotting a syringe close to our feet.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: Some are hidden under items, others are in plain sight.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: About 20 are collected to be destroyed.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: The team tells me this is exactly why they wear protective equipment.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: Meanwhile, a picture starts to emerge as letters with different names and addresses  - all miles outside the area - are fished out and photographed.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: Horan tells me if evidence which identifies a person is found, they will be questioned.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: If found liable, they could be fined if they have not properly undergone a "domestic duty of care".
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: "A lot of people think enviro-crime or fly-tipping is a victimless crime," Horan says.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: "It's not, there's many victims." Horan says people often employ a "man with a van" to dispose of their waste, but frequently the person hired just dumps it.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: If the waste is found dumped on private land, the owner will have to pay for its removal.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: Councils only pay if it is on public land.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: The team say fly-tipping costs the council thousands of pounds Wearing thick gloves, environmental enforcement officer Hanley continues to dig through the dump.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: I ask him about rogue waste removers and his advice for people wanting to get rid of waste.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: "I would advise people to take the right precautions, make sure that they're giving it to somebody who has a waste carriage licence," Hanley says.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: "Make sure that you're taking it to a proper waste facility if you're doing it yourself," he adds.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: The Environment Agency says waste criminals "scar our environment and communities".
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: It says: "Illegal waste dumping is a crime that costs the public purse £1bn a year.
sentences.article_title: The dump detectives on the trail of the fly-tippers

sentences.text: We know the challenges and are working hard to overcome them." It encourages the public to report suspected waste crime to its incident hotline or via its website.

sentences.text: Firefighters said this summer's wildfires were the worst they had experienced Firefighters and the public were knowingly put at risk during this year's wildfires due to chronic underfunding, a union has said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Those working on the ground and in the South Wales control centre said the fires were relentless with injuries "commonplace" for crews.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: The Fire Brigades Union (FBU) said firefighters were climbing hills in unsuitable boots and non-breathable layers used for house fires due to not having enough kit, and there was a "real risk to the public" if immediate action was not taken.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: The Welsh government said it did not provide core funding but "recognise the concerns raised and are clear that we need to do all we can to reduce the risk of wildfires".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Sean Cayford said some injured firefighters from the wildfires are still not back at work Sean Cayford, a firefighter in Bridgend, said crews were told in mid-August that there were no pumps or fire appliances available across the brigade's entire region.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "I've never heard that before but that was heard again later in the wildfire season.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: That was startling," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "We were stretched so thinly," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It has an increasingly destructive effect on the morale of our firefighters.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It's very difficult to be at a wildfire incident in excess of eight or 10 or 12 hours and not get injured to some degree." He said colleagues had sustained lower limb injuries and heat illness, with many still unable to work.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Gemma Thomas said control room staff were exhausted Gemma Thomas, who works in the control centre, said the average number of calls is usually 200-300 but on their busiest day this summer they had almost 2,000.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It was just relentless in there," she said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "There were times where we were unable to fulfil the requests that were coming from the incidents.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "We are the first point of contact for somebody who is having potentially the worst day of their life.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It was so stressful, mentally draining, that you're getting home from work absolutely shattered to think right I've got to go back and do it all again tomorrow." Thomas said there were times when staff needed to take breaks "one at a time for 10 minutes just to get people out of the room".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "People were getting to the point where they were just shattered in work, shattered at home," she said, adding there was no work-life balance because they needed to use free time to rest.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Thomas said support from management was "phenomenal" and "even the firefighters on the ground were understanding how stretched we were in the control room".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: But she does not believe they could sustain it long-term and wants to see an increase in numbers of firefighters.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: A wildfire above Cwm, Ebbw Vale, in August First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth held a climate change and resilience summit in Merthyr Tydfil on Thursday, which brought "key partners together to develop future actions".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: It hosted representatives from the fire services, police, local government, farmers and climate change organisations.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "There was poor preparation," said Gareth Tovey, executive council member for Wales, explaining they redirected specialist crews such as water teams to the wildfires.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "At some stages there was zero crew back up for vast parts of south Wales," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "Firefighters were injured because they didn't have the right kit to fight wildfires." The FBU said there was a shortfall of 400 firefighters in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Tovey said the union had been warning "for years" authorities needed to do something and there was a "real risk to the public" if immediate action was not taken.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: He said bringing in the Army , was "not a silver bullet" as they do not have the firefighting skills needed.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: An FBU survey following the fires found 69% of firefighters felt significantly under-equipped, with just 8% feeling fully equipped.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Nearly half reported welfare facilities during wildfire deployment were insufficient.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Firefighters are funded by the public but through a levy decided by the local authority for the area.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: This is part of their budget, which is in turn set by the Welsh government.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: North Wales Fire and Rescue Service was applying to the Welsh government's emergency assistance scheme to cover the additional cost of the wildfires this summer.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: While the full financial impact is still being assessed, the cost was expected to exceed £500,000.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: At one point firefighters in north Wales were managing six wildfires at once - more than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: It comes as a report from the UK's Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee said the wildfires left firefighters working in extreme conditions and exposed weaknesses in the UK's resilience and preparation.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: It called for a UK government-funded "national wildfire prevention campaign" with clear and consistent messaging, along with wildfire risk indicators in weather forecasts.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "This is a government now that is building that network of partners that showed real determination at the summit this morning to deal with what is clearly now a very very real challenge in the here and now." He declined to confirm there would be more funding.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "There is no escaping from the fact that we face very real financial challenges," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: The Welsh government said individual fire and rescue authorities determine how many firefighters they need and set their budgets accordingly.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "They should take this summer's wildfires into account when doing so," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service's chief fire officer Craig Flannery added climate-related emergencies were having a real impact on communities, environment and public services, and require a collective effort.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Natural Resources Wales' (NRW) national operations executive director, Dominic Driver, said: "The impacts of this summer's significant wildfires are still being felt across the country, going far beyond the visible scars left on the landscape.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "They can be seen in the habitats destroyed, carbon stores depleted and damaged soils that will take many years to regenerate and recover.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "We are focused on supporting nature's recovery and building resilience to this increasing challenge posed by climate change." He said NRW would be prioritising work to make Wales more climate-resilient.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires
