sentences.text: The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: As part of Wednesday's Budget, the government will commit £100m to establishing the new, "world first" institute with the support of leading AI firms.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: "AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," John Healey said.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: "I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: "One that doesn't leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country." The full details about the role and remit of the new lab are yet to emerge.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: But the AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said it would be a "major new global institution" that brings together "world-leading scientific expertise" to ensure the UK can safeguard its citizens and goals as AI develops.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: "That means staying ahead of emerging threats, from cyber attacks to biological risks, while building more of the critical technology our security depends on," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: Don't leave AI to tech bros and oligarchs, UK's AI minister says The Chancellor's plans to boost AI spending will also see an additional £120m committed to the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI).
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: Established by the former Conservative government in 2023, the lab evaluates the risks of the most advanced and powerful models - and has been championed for its role in helping build a collaborative and open approach to AI testing.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: The additional funding announced by the Chancellor will aim to help ensure the lab can continue its efforts and work, particularly amid growing calls for technical standards and guardrails for AI development.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: It will come alongside a £60m investment in what it coined a "National Cyber Shield" which it said would use agentic AI to boost cyber-defences, and £70m funding towards a National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability (NERV) Centre.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: This, it said, would harness AI tools to detect cyber vulnerabilities across the UK's critical infrastructure and economy.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: It comes after the UK government revealed it was among organisations around the world to have taken some sites offline as a precaution after critical flaws were surfaced in a popular programming language.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side scripting language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.text: But experts have warned that the incident shows how quickly and easily bugs which have lain long dormant may be surfaced - and potentially exploited - using AI.
sentences.article_title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab

sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Microsoft boss Satya Nadella says he has not seen anything like the PHP emergency "in a long, long time".
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Referencing the ongoing global efforts to fix the critical cyber-security flaw in millions of websites, he told a conference "it was a long day and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks".
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Other IT and cyber experts have told the BBC about their struggles in the last 48 hours, whose stories give us an insight into what it is like at the coalface of a major cyber emergency.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But also highlight how misinformation and panic has made things a lot worse.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "It's been relentless," says UK-based system administrator Adam Mudd.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said he had never had so many messages from people who were worried about their websites.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "The biggest challenge has been juggling clients who want their sites taken offline as a precaution, while trying to coordinate updates and fixes across countless different setups," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Sometimes it takes me longer to take a website down than to fix the PHP problem." PHP is a very popular programming language which powers millions of websites.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But two critical flaws were found with the system that led to the emergency response, with national cyber-security authorities urging IT teams to download a security fix urgently or take websites and servers offline.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Mudd says since then he has been under enormous pressure and has lost a huge amount of sleep - working early and not finishing until 22:30 BST to secure his customers' systems.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: In Mauritius, IT administrator Loganaden Velvindron said he too was flat out since his team realised just how much software relies on PHP.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Many versions of php running are completely end-of-life, so we are having to rebuilding web apps and change code in some cases," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said part of the problem was the announcement about the security vulnerabilities in PHP came as a surprise, without much time to prepare for action.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Jon Jones, Technical director for a digital advertising company, was also spurred into action by the alerts.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Seeing the warning drop was definitely eye-opening and a new experience we've not dealt with before," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "But, in a way, it was exciting feeling like a bit of a Hollywood action scene." The PHP Foundation, which manages the programming language, released its software fix and there was a scramble for people to download it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Jones said it felt like "the race was on" when the patch launched at 15:00 BST on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "It was also a bit nerve-racking as anyone who has applied software updates before would know, there's always a chance than an update can cause other issues," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: The rush came as someone had leaked details of the PHP flaw early - and it was heavily rumoured that cyber-criminals were already trying to carry out attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But cyber experts are also now questioning whether or not those rumours were real.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "We were flooded with rubbish intel about hackers being out there actively with working Proof of Concept (PoC) methods," said UK cyber expert Daniel Card.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said he also been flat out since Tuesday when the rumours of PHP hacks began circulating.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "This isn't the first time we've had a situation like this but it feels like it's been on another dimension," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He agreed that on paper the PHP vulnerabilities were very serious and should be taken seriously, but he and many others are frustrated with the misinformation about hackers being on the loose.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: As well as the alerts from government agencies - even the Prime Minister of Japan - cyber-security companies also made errors which didn't help.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: One major firm in this space issued warnings saying hackers had a working PoC - only to have to retract it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: In spite of warnings from Cloudflare and AWS that "millions of hacking attempts" had been made every hour, there is also no evidence of large scale data breaches or cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: It is true that hackers have been seen to use AI to attempt to build attack methods, but none of them seem to be working at scale at the moment - something that may well change soon.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: AI was also used to find the PHP flaws which had been hidden from human researchers for decades.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: The IT workers we spoke to all agreed that these kinds of serious flaws were going to be uncovered more frequently now that AI tools had become so good at hacking.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But some in the industry are concerned about how people were told about the critical vulnerabilities in PHP, as they fear improvements in AI will throw up more incidents like it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "We're going to find scary vulnerabilities with the amazing capabilities that OpenAI and Anthropic are bringing online, but we need to calibrate the messaging," posted Mark Maunder, founder of Wordfence - a Wordpress security tool.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in California was less than 1% , external each year.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Through what's known as a stock split announced by the company on Wednesday , Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Layoffs have continued into this year.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Major tech companies are set to spend an estimated $1 trillion , external this year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, like data centres .
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax

sentences.text: Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.

sentences.text: Sharon Osbourne spoke to BBC News as the family prepares to release a film about Ozzy's final concert with Black Sabbath It's been 15 months since Ozzy Osbourne died, at the age of 76, at his home in Buckinghamshire.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Although he had suffered from health problems for years, including Parkinson's disease and a fractured vertebra, his death was a shock.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Less than three weeks beforehand, he had been on stage in Birmingham, playing a triumphant farewell concert.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: After the show, he was on a high.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "He was just so, so happy," recalls his wife Sharon.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "He was online, going through the reviews and saying, 'There's something terribly wrong', and I'm like, 'Why?' "He goes, 'I didn't get slagged by anybody.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Why are people being nice to me?' "And I'm like, 'Because they like you'." On the morning he died, Ozzy had woken up early and gone downstairs for his usual morning workout.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Shortly afterwards, he had a heart attack.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: An air ambulance was called and paramedics tried to save him.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "I was asleep," says Sharon.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "We'd spoken in the night.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Ozzy had woken in the night and he asked me to kiss him twice, and I did.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "And then he said, 'Hold me, hold me tight,' and I did.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "And then the next thing I know, it's early in the morning, and someone comes rushing into the room saying, 'Come down now'.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "I ran down, and that was it." Sharon and Ozzy Osbourne, pictured in 2017 after renewing their wedding vows The grief, she says, will never leave.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "You've lost the love of your life, so you don't just wake up and go, 'I'm fine now.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: But you learn to live with it, and that's what I'm trying to do.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: So you either sit in a room and don't come out, or you accept it, befriend it, and that's it." The affection among Ozzy's fans was apparent before the singer's funeral.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Thousands of people lined the streets of Birmingham, laying floral tributes and singing Black Sabbath songs as Ozzy's body was transported through his home city in a hearse topped by a purple floral tribute in the shape of a cross.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Sharon says he would have been mystified by the outpouring of love.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "He'd have been like, 'What's the matter with you guys?
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: But for the family, the public response was a huge source of comfort.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "There was no way I could put Ozzy in a public graveyard," she says.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "I've seen what happens to other people in the public eye.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: There's no peace because people want to come and they want to pay their respects.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: That's an ongoing thing, and I wanted Ozzy to rest and just be." Does she visit him often?
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: I can see him from my window." She still talks to him regularly, she says.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Asked what she discusses, she puts a finger to her lips and gives a gentle "shh".
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Ozzy's family - including children Jack and Kelly - stopped to read the tributes during his funeral procession last July Ozzy and Sharon's relationship spanned more than 50 years.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: They met in 1970 and married in 1982.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Their time together could be turbulent - he was arrested for attempting to murder her in 1989 (she dropped the charges), and they split briefly in 2016 amid rumours of infidelity - but the couple maintained that they were soulmates.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "It was an unusual relationship because we had such highs and such terrible lows," she admits.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: But at the end of his life, "he knew" how much he was loved.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: You can see proof of that love - from his family, his fans and his bandmates – in a new documentary about his final gig at Birmingham's Villa Park last year, when he reunited with heavy rock legends Black Sabbath.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Titled Back To The Beginning, it features more than 25 of the songs played at that star-studded concert, including Ozzy's solo set and Sabbath's entire performance.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: In backstage footage, fellow A-list performers discuss the star's influence in awestruck tones.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "If there was no Sabbath, there's no Metallica," says the band's frontman James Hetfield.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "It's as simple as that." Yungblud, whose version of Changes was one of the concert's emotional high points, talks about how, as a kid who didn't fit in, Ozzy changed his life.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "The fact he was celebrated for his madness and his individuality gave me hope." sentences.text: But it almost never happened.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Six months before the show, Ozzy fell and fractured his vertebrae.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "They came to see us at the house and they said, 'You can't do this.

sentences.text: Your heart's too weak'," Sharon recalls.

sentences.text: But the singer was determined to see it through.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: In the film, it's hard to believe he's so ill.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Although he performs seated on a throne, his eyes are full of life and his voice is powerful.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: As he looks out at the crowd, he seems elated.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: Backstage, Sharon admits, "the whole family was terrified".
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: But something changed when Ozzy entered the stadium.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "He was sat in his dressing room, watching everybody on a screen performing, and he was like, 'I just can't believe they're all here'.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "It's amazing what support and love and determination can do for you, because [before the show] he was somebody that couldn't breathe.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: He had a heart condition.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: He had terrible, terrible agony from his spine.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: He had blood clots and he had Parkinson's.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "Some days just to even talk was an effort, let alone sing.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: And I don't know how he did it, but he did it.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: "And you saw it in his eyes, in his face.
sentences.article_title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'

sentences.text: It just made him feel like he was alive again." Ozzy is survived by Sharon, their three children (left-right: Kelly, Aimee and Jack) and three children from his previous marriage The effect was so galvanising that, when he came off stage, Ozzy declared he wanted to go on tour.

sentences.text: African diaspora is finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage A new sound is taking Bristol's dancefloors by storm.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Driven by rolling log drums, syncopated rhythms and infectious melodies, amapiano and other electronic sounds from across the African diaspora are finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Behind these parties is a new generation of black promoters passionate about creating spaces where black people can hear their music, celebrate their cultures and feel like they belong.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But for some, building these spaces has also meant confronting the familiar challenge of finding spaces where black music and the communities around it are welcomed and not feared.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Unkle Mykel started hosting events to connect to different cultures Bristol-based promoter Unkle Mykel's journey into events began in his own back garden after he moved to Bristol in 2017.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: What started as garden barbecues gradually grew into a way of bringing people together, particularly members of Bristol's black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's about celebrating our cultures, bringing people into that fold and connecting," says the 32-year-old, who hosts Bristol Barbecue Family and The Aux Social.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Originally from Kenya, Mykel moved to the UK in 2005.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Since then, he has witnessed changes in the visibility of African music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There was no Afrobeats on the airwaves," he laughs, recalling his early years in the country, when he says Caribbean reggae, dancehall and soca were more prominent in the musical landscape he encountered.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Now, he sees the growing popularity of genres such as amapiano - a popular South African house music subgenre - as an opportunity to broaden the scene.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We don't need to pretend to be nobody else, we're just us.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: It just took a while to get there." DJ and promoter Khiah Lou runs amapiano event called Khaya Nights For 30-year-old DJ and promoter Khiah Lou, representation, she says, is central to her work.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Last year she launched Khaya Nights, an event dedicated to amapiano and other African Caribbean electronic dance music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Having performed internationally, she had seen how other cities had developed a wider range of events celebrating these sounds.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Bristol, she felt, was lagging behind.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Rather than wait for the scene to develop, Khiah decided to help build it herself.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "If we don't do it, who else is going to do it?" she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Young black people are starting to make a way for themselves because I don't think we have a choice." Khiah says these nights provide a place where people can connect with their identities and see their cultures reflected in the city around them.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "At first it seems like it's just a party, but it's so much more than that," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's really important for your own self-identity.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: If your community doesn't have events, where do you feel you can go?" "At first it seems like just a party, but it's so much more than that,' says Khiah Tazmin Samuels, who DJs as Azumei, shares those concerns about representation.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: As part of Rushtown, a black-led music collective, Tazmin wants to champion sounds and subcultures from across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "My main motivation for getting together with people and starting Rushtown came from seeing the lack of representation of black music that black people are currently listening to within the city," says Tazmin.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: She sees encouraging signs, with more black music-focused brands emerging in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But she believes the wider music industry has yet to recognise the value of what these promoters are building.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Khiah says she has struggled to find venues willing to host nights aimed at black audiences.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Although she considers Bristol an inclusive city, her experience as a promoter has revealed a different side of its nightlife.

sentences.text: "I've had some venue owners straight up tell me they're worried about having a black event," she says.

sentences.text: "I feel like black crowds are kind of met with fear, and that's really disheartening." Mykel describes similar tensions, saying that some venues are enthusiastic about hosting his events, only to face objections from people in the surrounding community.

sentences.text: The Bamboo Club opened in 1966 as a social hub for Bristol's Caribbean community The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of  "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: In 1966, Tony Bullimore and his Jamaican-born wife Lalel, opened the Bamboo Club, which served as a cultural lifeline for the city's Caribbean community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Glen Crooks, 70, who used to perform at the Bamboo Club when he was younger, remembers "sneaking in" with his friends when they were young.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was the only place that we could have," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Especially all the Caribbean people could go and really have a good time." Rushtown aims to champion a variety of music genres from the African diaspora Marti Burgess, who has been a co-owner of the nightclub Lakota since 1994, says although attitudes have changed over the years, some prejudices remain.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There is a long history of treating a predominantly black audience as a concern, rather than recognising the audience, creativity and business that a promoter is bringing," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "They should not have to keep proving that black audiences are welcome or commercially worthwhile." Growing up, Marti was surrounded by music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Her parents went to the blues clubs and attended the Bamboo Club when it hosted artists such as Bob Marley, Desmond Dekker and Johnny Nash.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was through listening to the adults' conversations that I came to understand how much those spaces had grown out of exclusion from mainstream venues," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Latino Fest this summer opened our eyes further to the audiences and musical communities we could welcome," says Marti.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music
